label: USE CASE 20
title: How Crop Disease Detection Apps Work

scenes.text: A plant doctor in your pocket. A farmer notices strange spots on her tomato leaves. [1] She takes a photo with her phone, and within seconds, an app names the disease, and suggests what to do. [2] Let's break down how crop disease apps work.

title: Crop
Doctor AI
data.subtitle: A plant doctor in your pocket

scenes.text: Here's how it works. [1] The farmer photographs the affected leaf. [2] The app checks the photo is clear, and finds the leaf. [3] A vision model classifies the problem, like early blight, or healthy. [4] It gives a confidence score, like 92 percent sure, [5] and shows advice in the farmer's own language.

At its heart, it's image classification, from episode 29. [1] The model was trained on thousands of labelled leaf photos. [2] Healthy leaves, [3] leaves with different diseases and pests, [4] and leaves showing nutrient problems.

data.definition: A vision model that sorts a photo into one of several labels, like a disease name.

scenes.text: To really work for farmers, the app needs a few special features. [1] It works offline, with a small model on the phone, because fields often have weak signal. [2] It speaks local languages, with voice, for farmers who prefer listening. [3] And it connects to human experts, when the model isn't sure.

Here are four terms. [1] The dataset, the labelled photos it learned from. [2] Confidence, how sure the model is. [3] Edge AI, running the model on the phone itself. [4] And transfer learning, starting from a model trained on general photos, then teaching it about leaves.
So where does it help? [1] Farmers catch crop diseases early, and save their harvest. [2] Agriculture officers check many farms quickly. [3] And researchers track where diseases are spreading.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the app's answer is always right, so they can spray chemicals straight away. [2] It's a helpful first opinion, but similar looking diseases can confuse it. For serious problems, confirm with a local agriculture expert.

data.myth: The app is always right, so spray chemicals straight away.
data.fact: It's a helpful first opinion, but look-alike diseases can confuse it. Confirm serious cases with an expert.
